metadata.note: The Kennebec and Portland Railroad (opened 1849-1851) and its successor the Portland and Kennebec (1862-1870), the standard-gauge line Portland - Brunswick - Augusta with the Bath line (the original 1849 terminus), plus the Somerset & Kennebec (Augusta - Waterville - Skowhegan) worked by the P&K under lease 1864-1870, and the same corridor as the Maine Central's Lower Road 1870-1960. Drawn from research/branches/kennebec_and_portland_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-13; only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4: one feature per corridor per operator, sharing geometry - K&P to 1862, P&K 1862-1870, Maine Central from 1870. Not drawn here: the Somerset & Kennebec's own-name era before 1864; Maine Central Waterville - Skowhegan (separate Maine Central work); Amtrak's Downeaster (already in amtrak.geojson); Maine Eastern's Brunswick - Bath - Rockland seasonal trains (left to the Knox & Lincoln item).

properties.line: Kennebec and Portland: Portland – Yarmouth Junction
properties.speed_source: estimated, not computed from a timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py over ways tagged old_railway_operator=MEC (live CSX/Pan Am 'Portland Subdivision', 'Brunswick Branch', 'Waterville Subdivision', 'Hinckley Branch'; state-owned 'Rockland Branch'; out-of-service 'Lower Road Branch' and 'East Augusta Industrial Track'; lifted MEC grade Hinckley - Skowhegan) at 1x cost. Waypoints pinned onto the line itself at station sites, not taken from Nominatim (which returns township centroids in Maine).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 13.5 mi against a documented 13.5 mi (Fowler, Union Station MP 0 to Yarmouth Jct 13.5; about 15 mi from the Commercial Street datum). Operator mix: MEC 11.0 mi, (untagged) 2.5 mi ('(untagged)' = OSM rail on the same corridor without the MEC history tag). No straight-line leg; every waypoint lies on the drawn line. RULE 2 - LATER ALIGNMENT AT PORTLAND: the Portland end is drawn into the Union Station site (MP 0, St. John Street) on today's Portland Subdivision. Union Station opened in 1888; before that the road's Portland terminal was the Commercial Street station, about 1.6 mi further on (Wikipedia main-line datum). The pre-1888 approach to Commercial Street was not traced - its route from Deering Junction could not be established from OSM/OHM in this session - so for its whole 1850-1862 span this feature draws the post-1888 Union Station approach, not the line of its own era. Between Deering Junction and Yarmouth Junction the line follows today's Portland Subdivision and Brunswick Branch via Falmouth and the Cumberland area; the research report identifies this with the K&P's original route via Cumberland Center, but no separate K&P-era alignment was looked for.

segments.note: The K&P's own extension into Portland, opened 1850 (Wikipedia: 'Extension to Portland: 1850'); Westbrook, Falmouth and Cumberland all carry Fowler's letter x, i.e. they are in the 1850 Pathfinder Guide, so 1850 is primary-confirmed. Portland terminal was Commercial Street, not Union Station (1888). End 1862 is an ERA boundary, not an end of service: the company was reorganized as the Portland and Kennebec (incorporated 1862; Wikipedia gives formal consolidation 1 Jan 1864 - which name was on the timetable 1862-64 is not established). Standard gauge. Headway is an estimate; no source gives the number of trains in this era.
sources: Segment-level: start 1850 from Wikipedia ('Extension to Portland: 1850') and Fowler letter x (1850 Pathfinder) on Westbrook, Falmouth, Cumberland; end 1862 = K&P -> P&K reorganization (Wikipedia; 1862 vs 1864 unresolved). Headway NOT SOURCED.

properties.line: Portland and Kennebec: Augusta – Waterville (Somerset & Kennebec)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not computed from a timetable (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py over ways tagged old_railway_operator=MEC (live CSX/Pan Am 'Portland Subdivision', 'Brunswick Branch', 'Waterville Subdivision', 'Hinckley Branch'; state-owned 'Rockland Branch'; out-of-service 'Lower Road Branch' and 'East Augusta Industrial Track'; lifted MEC grade Hinckley - Skowhegan) at 1x cost. properties.geometry_quality: Traced 19.8 mi against a documented 19.3 mi (Fowler, Augusta 60.9 to Waterville 80.2). Operator mix: MEC 19.9 mi, (untagged) 0.0 mi ('(untagged)' = OSM rail on the same corridor without the MEC history tag). No straight-line leg; every waypoint lies on the drawn line. Crosses the Kennebec north of Augusta on the Maine Central bridge, follows the east bank on the 'East Augusta Industrial Track' via Riverside, Vassalboro and Winslow, runs up to the junction with the Waterville Subdivision at Winslow and crosses the Kennebec west into Waterville station; the 0.5 mi excess over the documented figure is mostly that junction wye. This is the Maine Central-era alignment; whether the Somerset & Kennebec's 1864-1870 route into Waterville used the same crossing was not checked.

segments.note: The Somerset & Kennebec, worked by the Portland and Kennebec under lease from 1 January 1864 (Wikipedia Skowhegan Branch and main-line articles). Fowler: Winslow and Waterville letter p (1856 Pathfinder). End 1870 is the Maine Central lease (Wikipedia Maine Central and main-line articles; the Skowhegan Branch article says 1871 - unresolved). Service continued under the Maine Central. Headway is an estimate; no source gives the number of trains in this era.

Fowler letter d (1954) on Bowdoinham, Richmond, South Gardiner, Gardiner, Hallowell, Augusta (Topsham's last letter is b, 1921 - a station closing, not a line closing). Last Maine Central passenger train 5 September 1960 (Wikipedia; another file gives the 6th - same year). Freight only afterwards; not drawn. Headway 180 is an estimate.

Waypoints pinned onto the line itself at station sites, not taken from Nominatim (which returns township centroids in Maine).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 19.8 mi against a documented 19.3 mi (Fowler, Augusta 60.9 to Waterville 80.2). Operator mix: MEC 19.9 mi, (untagged) 0.0 mi ('(untagged)' = OSM rail on the same corridor without the MEC history tag). No straight-line leg; every waypoint lies on the drawn line. Crosses the Kennebec north of Augusta on the Maine Central bridge, follows the east bank on the 'East Augusta Industrial Track' via Riverside, Vassalboro and Winslow, runs up to the junction with the Waterville Subdivision at Winslow and crosses the Kennebec west into Waterville station; the 0.5 mi excess over the documented figure is mostly that junction wye. Present-day alignment; no earlier one was looked for.

segments.note: Maine Central from its 1870 lease of the Portland & Kennebec and, through it, the Somerset & Kennebec (the Skowhegan Branch article says MEC leased both in 1871). Ran through to Bangor. Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 2 lists Vassalboro and Waterville (times not recoverable in this stretch); Fowler letter d (1954) on Vassalboro and Waterville; Winslow's last letter is c (1932), a station closing. Last Maine Central passenger train 5 September 1960 (Wikipedia; another file gives the 6th - same year). Freight only afterwards; not drawn. Headway 180 is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 8.2 mi against a documented 8.8 mi (Fowler 36.4; Feb 1952 Guide Table 5 prints Bath 36.3). Operator mix: MEC 8.3 mi ('(untagged)' = OSM rail on the same corridor without the MEC history tag). No straight-line leg; every waypoint lies on the drawn line. Ends at the Bath station site on the Rockland Branch; the 0.5 mi shortfall against Fowler's 36.4 is within the uncertainty of where each milepost datum sits at Brunswick and Bath (the Guide prints 36.3). Nothing east of Bath (Carlton Bridge, Woolwich) is drawn - that is the Knox & Lincoln's.

segments.note: Maine Central from the 1870 lease; the west end of its Rockland Branch once the Knox & Lincoln opened beyond Bath (train ferry across the Kennebec to 1927). Positive 1951 evidence: Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 5 prints rail times at Bath MP 36.3 and a through coach Rockland - Boston (the bus line is printed separately). Last regularly scheduled train 4 April 1959 (Wikipedia Rockland Branch / Downeaster articles). Freight only afterwards until Maine Eastern's seasonal trains (c. 2004-2015), which belong to the Knox & Lincoln / Rockland item and are not drawn here. Headway 360 is an estimate.
